I'll begin by discussing our notable
arrest and investigations. On September
25th, at approximately 1:00 a.m., uh,
Lndale Deputy Rally observed a male
Hispanic riding his bicycle and
conducted a traffic stop for several CVC
violations at Marine Avenue and Prairie
Avenue. When the deputy approached the
male suspect, he noticed he was carrying
a catalytic converter on his right
shoulder. He detained the suspect
pending a theft investigation. When the
deputy inspected the catalytic
converter, he noticed one end of the
vehicle part had been cut and altered
with an unknown tool. The deputy
attempted to interview the suspect
regarding the possible stolen vehicle
part, but he refused to speak with him.
The suspect was arrested and booked at
South LA station for reasonable cause
arrest grand theft. The suspect was a
resident of Lndale. On September 28th,
at approximately 900 pm, Deputy Felix
conducted a traffic stop at 153rd Street
and Hawthorne Boulevard on a vehicle for
CBC violations. He contacted the male
driver and female passenger of the
vehicle. The driver gave Deputy Felix
permission to search his vehicle, and
during the deputy's investigation, he
located a bag containing 15 fentanyl
pills in the backseat of the vehicle.
Both suspects were arrested and booked
at South LA station. They were charged
with possession of a controlled
substance for sales. Neither suspect was
a resident of Lndale.
During this reporting period, Lndale
deputies made four misdemeanor narcotic
arrests for possession of various types
of narcotics and possession of drug
paraphernalia.
Regarding our traffic related incidents,
traffic enforcement deputy Gomez issued
18 citations during the reporting period
for various vehicle code violations such
as failure to stop at a stop sign,
failure to stop at a red light, and
speeding.
Lastly, I would like to invite everyone
to our next neighborhood watch meeting,
Wednesday, October 21st, starting at 6
p.m. located at Harold Hoffman Community
Center. Come out, enjoy some time with
your local deputies and community
members. This concludes my report and
I'd be happy to answer any questions.

Incredibly, until September 15, 2025,
the city of Lawndale claims to have not
had a written policy regarding how the
mayor and council members could spend
their 2500 annual discretionary
allocation. I re reviewed records
showing how these funds were spent over
approximately the past two years. Most
of the expenditures by this body raised
no particular concern, but council
member Tala's expenditures deserve
closer examination. Here is a chronology
of concerning expenditures.
March 3rd, 2025, 300
lapel pins were purchased. June 10th,
2025, six shirts and two jackets were
purchased from Land's End. September 15,
2025, a 500 donation, $500 donation was
made to the South Bay social network.
May 21st, 2026, another nine shirts were
purchased. That is 17 articles of
clothing in less than a year paid for
with public money. The September 15,
2025 date is particularly interesting
because that that is also the date the
city's new discretionary funds policy
was established. This the policy
specifically permits the purchase of
Londale branded clothing that is not
included in the adopted budget. Yet the
clothing purchased by council members
Calver was not Londale branded. The
timing raises a legitimate question. Was
this provision added in response to or
influenced by clothing purchases that
had already been made by council member
Taloa? If that is not the reason that
the council should be able to provide
the reason for spec specifically adding
this provision to the policy and I think
that council should also answer another
question. The lapel pins and 17 articles
of clothing provide a legitimate public
benefit sufficient to justify spending
taxpayer dollars? Fortunately, the
council did not approve the proposal to
increase the discretionary fund from
2500 to 3500 that Tal requested, but the
clothing is not my greatest concern. On
September 15, 2025, the same day this
funds policy was adopted, Councilman
Tala submitted a request to finance for
$500 donation to the South Bay social
network, a nonprofit based in Gardina.
The organization spec subsequently
endorsed Calivary in his campaign for
mayor. I believe the circumstances raise
a serious appearance of conflict and
public funds concerned that deserves
scrutiny. If a public official uses just
discretionary taxpayer funds to make a
contribution to a nonprofit organization
and that organization later endorses
that same official for mayor, the public
has every right to ask whether the
expenditure served a legitimate
municipal purpose and whether the
arrangement complied with the applicable
nonprofit and campaign finance
requirements. There are other cities
that have much more restrictive
discretionary fund policies. For
example, the policy used by KDA where a
currency manager briefly worked provides
significantly greater controls including
a specific approval process and
documentation requirements. I believe
the law should consider adopting similar
lifeguards and ocular policies to
current council members expenditures.
Thank you.
